_comment: Proposed additions to the artifact model. Applied by the generator on top of daydor_model.json. Push these back into the artifact so it stays the single source of truth.

columns.name: requested_by_user_id
columns.reason: Maker-checker: the database must know who raised the request to stop the same person approving it.

columns.name: requested_by_agent_run_id
columns.reason: Maker-checker for agent-raised requests; links the gate to the agent run that computed the subject.

columns.name: decision_note
columns.reason: Approver's reason, needed for audit of rejections and overrides.

grant_caps.reason: Finding 2: the artifact gives the employee role W on every employee column, so an employee could set their own is_active, date_of_exit, legal_entity_id (payroll derives the tax jurisdiction from it), department_id, position_id or date_of_joining. Employees keep self-service on personal_address only; every other column is HR-owned and changes through employee-record-writer or tenant_hr.
Finding 23: timecards are built by punch-validator and approved by the manager through g_timecard; an employee could set their own status and approved_by_user_id.
Finding 23: an employee submits the claim (category, receipt) but must not set policy flags, link their own approval, or mark it reimbursed / posted.
Finding 23: an employee asks for leave (policy, dates, reason) but must not approve it, set the FMLA designation (g_fmla) or link their own approval.
Finding 23: carrier transmission is system state, written by carrier-file-transmitter.
Finding 23: checklists are built by onboarding/termination builders; an employee could mark their own offboarding checklist complete.
Finding 23: an employee reports the event and evidence; qle-validator owns the status and enrollment window.
Finding 23: assignments and completion are written by the training agents; an employee could assign or complete their own mandatory training.
